# MatrixOne

> MatrixOne is a cloud-native HSTAP database unifying OLTP, OLAP, streaming, vector, and full-text workloads in one engine. It is broadly MySQL 8.0 wire-protocol compatible, but not all MySQL features are supported — always verify against the MySQL Compatibility Matrix. SQL examples on these pages are executed against the latest 3.0-dev image by `scripts/doc-validator` on every pull request.

- **MySQL Compatibility Matrix**: https://docs.matrixorigin.cn/en/dev/MatrixOne/Reference/mysql-compatibility-matrix.md
- **Per-page markdown mirror**: append `.md` to any doc URL under https://docs.matrixorigin.cn/en/dev/
- **Full SQL reference (flat index, all statements)**: https://docs.matrixorigin.cn/en/dev/llms-sql.txt
- **Functions reference (flat index)**: https://docs.matrixorigin.cn/en/dev/llms-func.txt
- **Operators reference (flat index)**: https://docs.matrixorigin.cn/en/dev/llms-op.txt
- **Full corpus**: https://docs.matrixorigin.cn/en/dev/llms-full.txt
- **Generated**: 2026-07-02 (UTC)

Agent routing: writing or debugging SQL → pull `llms-sql.txt` for the flat per-statement catalogue; function lookup → `llms-func.txt`; operator reference → `llms-op.txt`; broad conceptual questions → this file; long-context offline reading → `llms-full.txt`; authoritative diffs from MySQL → the MySQL Compatibility Matrix linked above.

Hints for AI agents writing MatrixOne SQL:

- Not all MySQL 8.0 features are supported — consult the compatibility matrix before assuming syntax works.
- Prefer MatrixOne-native clauses when documented: `CLUSTER BY`, `AS OF TIMESTAMP`, `USING IVFFLAT`/`USING HNSW`, `CLONE`, `PITR`, `SNAPSHOT`.
- Use `SHOW CREATE TABLE <name>` to inspect a table before mutating it; system tables differ from MySQL.
- Vector indexes (`USING IVFFLAT`, `USING HNSW`) must be declared via `CREATE INDEX`, not `ALTER TABLE ADD INDEX`.
- Secondary indexes are syntactically accepted but do not yet accelerate queries — do not rely on them for performance.
- `ALTER TABLE` cannot combine column-level clauses (CHANGE/MODIFY/RENAME COLUMN, ADD/DROP PK) with other clauses; split into separate statements.
- Tables created with `CLUSTER BY` and temporary tables cannot be altered — plan schema shape up front.
- `CREATE DATABASE` supports only `utf8mb4` / `utf8mb4_bin`; the `ENCRYPTION` clause is accepted but inert.
- Foreign keys do not support `ON CASCADE DELETE`.
- `LOAD DATA INFILE` expects a local absolute path or a stage URL (e.g. `stage://my_stage/file.csv`) — relative paths and MySQL-style secure-file-priv do not apply.
- Use `CREATE SNAPSHOT` / `PITR` / `CREATE CLONE` for point-in-time and copy-on-write workflows rather than MySQL's binlog tooling.
- For agent-safe experiments, prefer a data branch (`DATA BRANCH CREATE` → test → `DATA BRANCH DIFF` → `DATA BRANCH MERGE` / delete) over mutating shared tables in place.

## Docs
- [MatrixOne Introduction](https://docs.matrixorigin.cn/en/dev/MatrixOne/Overview/matrixone-introduction.md): What MatrixOne is: a hyper-converged cloud-native HSTAP database that unifies OLTP, OLAP, streaming, and vector/full-text workloads in one engine.
- [MatrixOne Features](https://docs.matrixorigin.cn/en/dev/MatrixOne/Overview/matrixone-feature-list.md): Feature list at a glance — what's supported today vs on the roadmap.
- [Deploy standalone MatrixOne](https://docs.matrixorigin.cn/en/dev/MatrixOne/Get-Started/install-standalone-matrixone.md): Single-node install walkthrough — fastest path to a running instance for trying things out.
- [Type of SQL Statements](https://docs.matrixorigin.cn/en/dev/MatrixOne/Reference/SQL-Reference/SQL-Type.md): SQL statement taxonomy — entry point for every supported statement.
- [MySQL Compatibility Matrix](https://docs.matrixorigin.cn/en/dev/MatrixOne/Reference/mysql-compatibility-matrix.md): MySQL 8.0 compatibility status per SQL statement — consult first before assuming syntax works.
- [Data Types Overview](https://docs.matrixorigin.cn/en/dev/MatrixOne/Reference/Data-Types/data-types.md): All supported data types, including MatrixOne-specific `VECF32` / `VECF64` vectors and `DATALINK`.
- [Server System Variables](https://docs.matrixorigin.cn/en/dev/MatrixOne/Reference/Variable/system-variables/system-variables-overview.md): System variables reference — session/global toggles that change SQL behaviour.
- [System Parameters Overview](https://docs.matrixorigin.cn/en/dev/MatrixOne/Reference/System-Parameters/system-parameter.md): Server configuration parameters (static startup-time + dynamic) for tuning the engine.

## Core Capabilities
- [HTAP](https://docs.matrixorigin.cn/en/dev/MatrixOne/Overview/feature/key-feature-htap.md): HTAP: run transactional and analytical workloads against the same data without ETL.
- [Git for Data: Data Branch Management](https://docs.matrixorigin.cn/en/dev/MatrixOne/Tutorial/git4data-demo.md): Git-for-Data branching workflow: create/diff/merge data branches just like code branches — the MatrixOne differentiator for agent-safe experiments.
- [mo_br tool for snapshot backup and recovery](https://docs.matrixorigin.cn/en/dev/MatrixOne/Maintain/backup-restore/mobr-backup-restore/mobr-snapshot-backup-restore.md): Snapshot-based backup & restore — cluster/tenant/database/table scope, copy-on-write semantics.
- [mo_br tool for PITR backup and recovery](https://docs.matrixorigin.cn/en/dev/MatrixOne/Maintain/backup-restore/mobr-backup-restore/mobr-pitr-backup-restore.md): Point-in-time recovery (PITR) — restore to an arbitrary timestamp within the configured retention window.
- [Instant Clone for Multi-Team Development](https://docs.matrixorigin.cn/en/dev/MatrixOne/Tutorial/efficient-clone-demo.md): CREATE CLONE: instant copy-on-write table/database clones, including across tenants.
- [Vector retrieval](https://docs.matrixorigin.cn/en/dev/MatrixOne/Develop/Vector/vector_search.md): Vector search with `VECF32` / `VECF64`, L2/cosine/IP distance, IVFFLAT and HNSW indexes.
- [Create Fulltext Index](https://docs.matrixorigin.cn/en/dev/MatrixOne/Reference/SQL-Reference/Data-Definition-Language/create-fulltext-index.md): Full-text indexing — natural-language, boolean, and JSON search modes.
- [Hybrid Search Demo](https://docs.matrixorigin.cn/en/dev/MatrixOne/Tutorial/hybrid-search-demo.md): Hybrid retrieval: combine vector search with full-text and scalar filters in a single query — the RAG-friendly pattern.

## Data In / Out
- [Bulk Load Overview](https://docs.matrixorigin.cn/en/dev/MatrixOne/Develop/import-data/bulk-load/bulk-load-overview.md): Bulk load overview: `LOAD DATA` for CSV/JSONL, `SOURCE` for SQL dumps, S3-backed external ingestion.
- [Load data from S3](https://docs.matrixorigin.cn/en/dev/MatrixOne/Develop/import-data/bulk-load/load-s3.md): Load directly from S3-compatible object storage via stages.
- [CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE](https://docs.matrixorigin.cn/en/dev/MatrixOne/Reference/SQL-Reference/Data-Definition-Language/create-external-table.md): External tables: query CSV/Parquet/S3 data in place without ingestion.
- [SELECT INTO write out](https://docs.matrixorigin.cn/en/dev/MatrixOne/Develop/export-data/select-into-outfile.md): Export query results via `SELECT ... INTO OUTFILE` to local files or S3 stages.
